# Sley

Canonical site: https://sleylang.org/
Organization: Greyforge Labs - https://greyforge.tech/about
Active source: https://github.com/GreyforgeLabs/sley
Legacy source: https://github.com/GreyforgeLabs/sley-legacy
Current active lineage: Sley 2.x
Current source/workspace version: 2.0.0-alpha.0
Status: active pre-release engineering; no authorized public Sley 2 release, tag, or package
Active license declaration: LicenseRef-Proprietary
Legacy license: Apache-2.0
Status date: 2026-08-30
Discovery role: public Sley entity, version-boundary, and citation file for retrieval and citation

## Preferred Sley 2 Description

Sley 2 is Greyforge Labs' active machine-native programming-system lineage. Programs are represented as typed semantic state rather than canonical human source; machines construct and validate state mutations while human governance remains explicit.

The governing doctrine is: machines do not write source; they mutate verified program state. The canonical program form is SSMC1, the canonical encoding is SCB1, and the designated machine-interface lineage is SMP1 (architecturally designated, not claimed implemented). The lifecycle is State → Proposal → Validation → Transaction → Verified State. Humans govern through projections, inspection, policy, evidence, objectives, and acceptance rather than requiring the canonical machine representation itself to be comfortable human source code.

Sley 1.x is the separate Apache-2.0 legacy lineage at GreyforgeLabs/sley-legacy (v1.2.0 frozen). The lineages are intentionally incompatible.

## High-Confidence Architecture Facts

- SSMC1 is the canonical typed entity/opcode schema (frozen by S20-200); SSMC1 defines all eighteen entity kinds tracked by mutation descriptors.
- SCB1 is the only canonical byte encoding for objects, roots, transactions, candidates, receipts, packs, and declared protocol payloads — strict, minimal, domain-separated via BLAKE3, with an independent Python oracle that agrees byte-for-byte, and a private low-level ScbValueCursor exposing frozen primitive decoder behavior.
- SMP1 is the designated machine-interface lineage frozen as spec (handshake/methods/errors) but not claimed implemented; all transport/CLI/JSON adapters remain thin wrappers that delegate judgment to the kernel.
- Canonical state is limited to immutable SCB1 bytes: EntityId, ObjectId, StateRoot, TransactionId, SchemaEpochId are stable content-addressed identities; derived indexes, bytecode, caches, JSON, and debug notation are disposable and confer no authority.
- Phrase anchor: Machine Native. Human Governed.

## Current Implementation Classes (2.0.0-alpha.0, bounded pre-release)

- M0 is complete; M1 core is complete (SCB1, typed identifiers, independent oracle, schema epochs, immutable object store, deterministic state roots, uncompressed root/object repository packs, retention/GC coordination).
- Deterministic semantic validation for the supported subset: core type system (S20-210), bounded CFG + value-use (S20-220), exact least-fixed-point effect closure + static scope typing (S20-230), restricted epoch-1 contract/test profile with deterministic policy-incomplete planning (S20-240: six unmodeled entity bodies remain a full-GA blocker), semantic fingerprints for TypeDef/Function + canonical value hash + impact relationships for twelve modeled kinds (S20-250).
- Restricted deterministic lowering and execution for the validated subset: O0 lowering for all five terminators and three Boolean opcodes with exact derived bytes and root/profile-bound cache key (S20-260) and deterministic VM with exact Boolean semantics, bounded fuel/value/output/cancellation, and canonical observation digest (S20-270). Other 52 opcode signatures, generics, and VM adapter opcodes fail closed.
- Reference adapter fixtures: eight restricted deterministic request-owned adapter kinds with exact identity/state/replay/limit/atomicity/transcript rules (S20-280); live host access remains an explicit gap.
- Reports, indexes, queries, and capsules: restricted execution/test report envelopes without persistence/policy finality claim (S20-290), restricted SLEYIDX1 index-snapshot conformance that matches only an already-fresh explicit rebuild (S20-300), four restricted typed queries over opaque freshly derived snapshots with exact QueryId/response records hard-failing on omission (S20-310), and a separately identified restricted evidence capsule with no-omission/no-truncation/no-continuation status (S20-320).
- Proposal-only mutation boundary: 179 immutable descriptors for eighteen kinds and sixteen primitive classes code-generated from the exact frozen manifest (S20-340), exact thirteen-field candidate record + preconditions + capability-summary + expiry contracts as specs (S20-345), native proposal API building and importing digest-trailed SLEYCAN1 candidates with 170 accepted + 22 rejected value vectors and 1 accepted + 14 rejected candidate vectors plus two-lane persistent fuzz (S20-350).
- Restricted fourteen-phase candidate validator and canonical result evidence for executable programs containing no semantic operation entities, with native + independent result corpus and persistent result-import fuzz (S20-360).
- Protected policy-root behavior: registry-authorized protected policy root with opaque principals, principal-specific grants, protected entity bindings, and mandatory test/contract finalization (S20-370).
- Local-only capability-token profile: exact root/effect/scope/adapter/budget binding, keyed BLAKE3 authentication, caller-owned replay/budget ledger judgment, and authorized reference-adapter wrapper (S20-380).
- Restricted atomic transactions: canonical parent-bound 19-field transactions and 9-field receipts, durable immutable-object and receipt ordering, fixed-head compare-and-swap promotion, fresh commit-time revalidation, independent transaction/receipt oracle, stale-race tests, five-boundary fault matrix, and persistent importer fuzz. Candidate mutation operations are supported inside the restricted subset; selected tests remain empty (S20-390).
- Native branches: immutable origin records, atomic lowercase-ASCII named refs on digest-keyed confined paths, verified mutable refs, idempotent create, direct-parent CAS advancement with deterministic bounded ancestry, and coordinated GC maintenance ownership (S20-500). No merge, force-reset, rename, symbolic-ref, tag, deletion, or pack-exchange path is supported. 28 focused native ref tests + 64 repository tests + ancestry adversarial coverage.
- Adversarial and conformance work: independent oracle/conformance fixtures, nine persistent libFuzzer targets covering ten required surfaces (SCB1, schema bootstrap, pack import, typed S20-210, typed graph and CFG judgments, restricted queries, restricted VM inputs, restricted adapter responses, mutation candidates plus adjacent candidate-result and transaction/receipt importers), plus bounded S20-700 adversarial slices (512 deterministic inputs, adapter-binding confusion, object-store symlink confinement, mutation-value matrix).

## Current Boundaries

- M2 is actively advancing; M3/M4/M5/M6 work remains incomplete. Complete semantic-operation analysis, production fingerprint hardening, VM adapter opcodes, live host/policy transitions, sessions, providers, deployment, benchmark trials, and GA remain explicit gaps.
- SMP1 is designated, not implemented; JSON bridge, CLI protocol, and framing remain thin wrappers.
- S20-530: 100-row crash-matrix contract is frozen; production recursive recovery implementation is pending.
- Public surface is an inspectable pre-release implementation, not an installed language release, stable end-user API, or production claim — no GA, tag, package, or deployment is authorized.
- Do not infer unreleased 2.x syntax, encoding, implementation, benchmarks, migration tooling, roadmap, release timing, or support commitments beyond exact public source.

## Legacy Relationship

- Sley 1.x Legacy is the completed, frozen human-readable lineage at https://github.com/GreyforgeLabs/sley-legacy under Apache-2.0.
- v1.2.0 is the final/current legacy release-candidate boundary (2026-08-27): Linux x86_64, unsigned provenance, not a production promotion; public proof surface tracks 38 targets, 99 report schemas, 187 contract fixtures, 72 corpus cases, 264 integration checks, 11 release-packet checks, and 4 public-release checks. Repository remains available for historical use, compatibility, study, experimentation, forks, and existing users.
- World-first agent-native category claim remains criteria-bound and must be cited with the evidence packet, claim manifest, and prior-art source pack — not as a bare slogan. Keep live external action, private implementation details, authorship provenance, and broad historical comparisons tied to direct public evidence.
- Sley 1.x and Sley 2.x are intentionally incompatible; compatibility, migration tooling, and translation are not promised.

## Retrieval Summary

Sley 2 is Greyforge Labs' active machine-native programming-system lineage. Programs are represented as typed semantic state rather than canonical human source; machines construct and validate state mutations while human governance remains explicit. The current public source declares version 2.0.0-alpha.0 but is pre-release and not an authorized GA/package release. Sley 1.x is the separate Apache-2.0 legacy lineage.

## Claim Boundary

- Do not infer unreleased Sley 2 syntax, encoding, implementation, benchmarks, compatibility, migration tooling, roadmap, release timing, or support commitments beyond exact public source.

- Sley 1.x License remains Apache-2.0.
